sections.heading: Section 1: Resolving Forces in Two Dimensions

questions.q: A force of magnitude 50 N acts at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components.
Two forces $F_1 = [8, -3]$ N and $F_2 = [-5, 7]$ N act on a particle. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
questions.answer: Resultant $\mathbf{R} = F_1 + F_2 = [8 - 5, -3 + 7] = [3, 4]$ N. Magnitude $|\mathbf{R}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A particle is held in equilibrium by three coplanar forces: $P$ acting East, $Q$ acting North, and a force of 13 N acting at an angle $\theta$ South of West where $\tan\theta = 5/12$. Find the magnitude of $P$.
questions.answer: For equilibrium, horizontal components balance: $P = 13\cos\theta$. Since $\tan\theta = 5/12$, $\cos\theta = 12/13$, so $P = 13(12/13) = 12\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A block of mass 6 kg rests on a rough horizontal table where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.35$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, what is the maximum frictional force that can act on the block?
questions.answer: Normal reaction $R = mg = 6(10) = 60\text{ N}$. Maximum static friction $F_{\text{max}} = \mu R = 0.35(60) = 21\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A horizontal force of 15 N is applied to the 6 kg block in the previous question (where $F_{\text{max}} = 21\text{ N}$). What is the actual frictional force acting on the block?
questions.answer: Since the applied force (15 N) is less than the limiting friction (21 N), the block remains at rest and friction balances the applied force: $F = 15\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A particle of mass 4 kg is placed on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. If the particle is on the point of slipping down the plane, find the coefficient of friction $\mu$.
questions.answer: At limiting equilibrium on an incline, $\mu = \tan\alpha$. For $\alpha = 30^\circ$, $\mu = \tan(30^\circ) = 1/\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3}/3 \approx 0.577$.

questions.q: A crate of mass 10 kg is held in equilibrium on a smooth slope inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal by a force $P$ acting parallel to the slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, find $P$.
questions.answer: Resolving parallel to the slope: $P = mg\sin(30^\circ) = 10(10)(0.5) = 50\text{ N}$.

questions.q: For the crate in the previous question, what is the normal contact force exerted by the slope on the crate?
questions.answer: Resolving perpendicular to the slope: $R = mg\cos(30^\circ) = 100(\sqrt{3}/2) = 50\sqrt{3} \approx 86.6\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A body of mass 8 kg rests in limiting equilibrium on an inclined plane. The normal reaction is 64 N. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, find the angle of inclination $\alpha$ of the plane.
A lamp of weight $W = 60\text{ N}$ is suspended by two light strings making angles of $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with the horizontal ceiling. Find the tension in the steeper string.
questions.answer: The angles with the vertical are $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$. The two strings are perpendicular ($30^\circ + 60^\circ = 90^\circ$). Resolving along the steeper string: $T_2 = W\cos(30^\circ) = 60(\sqrt{3}/2) = 30\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 52.0\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A light inextensible string passes over a smooth peg. A mass of 5 kg hangs on one side and a mass of 3 kg hangs on the other. What downward external force must be applied to the 3 kg mass to maintain equilibrium? ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.answer: Tension in string is $T = 5g = 50\text{ N}$. On the 3 kg side: $T = 3g + F \Rightarrow 50 = 30 + F \Rightarrow F = 20\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A ring of mass $m$ is threaded on a rough horizontal wire with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.4$. A light string attached to the ring is pulled with tension $T$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the wire. Find the value of $T$ (in terms of $mg$) when the ring is in limiting equilibrium.
questions.answer: Resolving vertically: $R + T\sin(45^\circ) = mg \Rightarrow R = mg - T\sin(45^\circ)$. Horizontal friction: $F = \mu R = 0.4(mg - T\sin(45^\circ))$. For limiting equilibrium: $T\cos(45^\circ) = 0.4(mg - T\sin(45^\circ)) \Rightarrow T(\cos 45^\circ + 0.4\sin 45^\circ) = 0.4mg \Rightarrow T = \frac{0.4mg}{1.4(\sqrt{2}/2)} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{7}mg$.
